answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the self-serve funnel, and onboarding friction is upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly moves both. Two independent inherited records (memory_31 on signup field reduction, memory_86 on shortened onboarding) converge on that lever, which makes it the best-supported single slot. I verify memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the intended action and its summary states no effect size, duration, or segment scope; I verify memory_91 because activation messaging is the strongest alternative for the same slot and I want the comparison grounded before committing. I deliberately reject promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that a 40% SMB discount bought signup (+31%) and short-run revenue (+18%) while costing 12pp of monthly retention, which is exactly the trade the primary objective forbids; competitive pressure is the situation that makes that lever tempting, not evidence that it now works. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the observed funnel decline; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment than the one that is bleeding. Downstream value risk: removing signup fields and onboarding steps can strip qualification data and route enterprise-shaped prospects into self-serve, which memory_44 says converts worse on pipeline quality, and can inflate activation counts with accounts that never become qualified revenue. So the test must be gated on downstream qualified-revenue and retention guardrails, not activation alone, and enterprise-signal prospects should still be diverted to the demo-request path. Uncertainty that survives: all six memories are lossy consolidations of archived records, memory_73 is compressed to the point of hiding whether the retention loss was discount-specific or price-change-specific, and none of the prior wins were measured under a competitor price shock, so their effect sizes may not transfer.
